h1: The 6 Best Desktop Safes of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six compact safes for desks and home offices, compared on mounting, capacity and access, with a pick for every budget.
summary: The Amazon Basics Steel Security Safe is the best desktop safe, with four expansion bolts, an adjustable removable shelf and an electronic keypad. The Bonsaii offers the most room at 0.6 cu ft with a USB-C backup. The slim Amazon Basics drawer safe hides away, the 4.6 L dual-code box suits shared desks, and the MAESTON and Yuanshikj are small budget boxes.
intro: A safe that sits loose on a desk is a tidy box for a thief to carry out the door. What separates real protection from a decorative lock box is whether it can be fixed down, and the first line to read on any listing is the mounting hardware. Bolts through the desk or the floor turn a ninety-second grab into a job that needs tools and noise.

Six desk-sized safes are ranked here from spec sheets. Mounting hardware, interior layout and access method decided the order, and every pick supplies a way to anchor it or fit it inside a drawer. Capacity came next, then backup access, since a keypad that dies with its batteries is an expensive paperweight. We say where a listing leaves the important details out.

products.name: Amazon Basics Steel Security Safe and Lock Box with Electronic Keypad
products.verdict: The most reconfigurable, genuinely anchorable desktop safe.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics Steel Security Safe comes with the bolts that make it a safe. It ships with four expansion bolts, has an adjustable, removable interior shelf, an electronic keypad and three indicator lights that show what the lock is doing, at $50 to $100. Expansion bolts bite into a desk, wall or floor material, which is the difference between a safe and a box.

It wins because it combines bolt-down hardware with the flexible interior that cheaper boxes lack. Against the Bonsaii below, it gives up capacity for layout control.

Buy it if you want a safe you can reorganize and fix in place. The caveats are the price, which is higher than the budget picks, and the keypad, which needs batteries: replace them on a schedule and keep a record, so you are not locked out. Check what your desk is made of.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want an anchored, configurable safe.

products.name: Bonsaii Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Home Office, 0.6 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: The largest anchorable safe here, with a USB-C backup.
products.description:
The Bonsaii is the roomy one. It offers 0.6 cubic feet with mounting hardware included, a removable shelf for organizing, and three ways in, including a USB-C backup, at $50 to $100. The backup is the thoughtful part: if batteries die, a USB-C power source can wake the keypad and let you open the door.

It sits just behind the Amazon Basics Steel because it trades a sturdier-looking bolt kit for more space. It beats the smaller boxes below on room, and a removable shelf lets a laptop or a stack of papers fit.

A good fit for a home office that stores documents and devices. The caveat is footprint: it takes more desk or floor space than the mini safes, and the price bucket is higher than the budget boxes, so skip it if desk space is tight.
products.idealFor: Home offices storing documents and devices.

products.name: Amazon Basics Small Slim Desk Drawer Security Safe with Programmable Electronic
products.verdict: A slim safe that fits in a drawer or on the desktop.
products.description:
The slim Amazon Basics desk drawer safe lets you hide the safe. It has a slim profile with mounting hardware included, and it fits inside a drawer or on the desktop. A programmable electronic keypad is backed by an emergency key, at $50 to $100. A safe inside a drawer is invisible to a casual visitor, which is a security gain in itself.

It ranks third because the slim shape cuts capacity compared with the two above, in return for flexible placement.

Best for people who want the choice to hide it. The caveat is depth: check interior dimensions for what you need to store, because a slim box may not take a passport folder or a tablet. A drawer safe also needs a drawer that locks or sits out of sight, and mounting it to the drawer base is wise.
products.idealFor: People who might hide the safe in a drawer.

products.name: Digital Electronic Money Safe, Steel Security Lock Box with Keypad, Office
products.verdict: A 4.6 liter SPCC steel box with two codes and 18mm bolts.
products.description:
The dual-code money safe is the shared desk pick. It has a 4.6 liter interior in SPCC steel with 18mm dual locking bolts, a peg-mounting system for concealed placement and support for two independent access codes, at $25 to $50. Two codes mean two people can each have their own without sharing a single passcode.

It places fourth because the interior is smaller than the Bonsaii's, but two codes suit shared desks and the bucket is lower. The 18mm bolts add resistance to prying.

Good for two people sharing a workspace, such as partners or small-office staff. The caveat is the 4.6 liter interior, which holds cash and small items rather than documents, and the keypad means batteries are involved. Plan to replace them and keep an emergency method of access.

products.name: MAESTON Mini Electronic Safe Box with Digital Keypad & Keys, 0.23 Cubic
products.verdict: A small anchorable box with a 3 to 8 digit custom code.
products.description:
The MAESTON is a small box for a desk corner. It has a customizable 3 to 8 digit password, mounting hardware, a magnetic auto-lock door and a small footprint, at $25 to $50. A longer code is harder to guess, and the magnetic door closes itself so you cannot forget to shut it.

It trails the dual-code safe on locking hardware, with no stated bolt rating, but gives a longer code option.

It works for small valuables in a corner: spare keys, a passport, jewelry. The magnetic door also helps if you are in a hurry. The caveat is capacity, limited to 0.23 cubic feet, and a keypad that needs batteries. If you store anything bulky, move up to the Bonsaii. A box this small fills quickly.
products.idealFor: Small valuables kept in a desk corner.

products.name: Yuanshikj Small Steel Security Safe Box with Keypad, Key, 0.23 CuFt, Black
products.verdict: The cheapest bucket with mounting hardware included.
products.description:
The Yuanshikj is the budget safe that still bolts down. It includes mounting hardware, measures 9.05 by 6.69 by 6.69 inches and has a magnetic auto-lock door, under $25. Being able to anchor a safe at the lowest price bucket matters more than extra features for a student or renter.

It finishes last only because it offers fewer features than the safes above, though it is the lowest bucket here. The basic keypad design is simple to operate.

It suits students and budget buyers who still want to bolt a safe down. The caveat is a plain feature set, with battery dependence and no backup port. Keep spare batteries on hand, and do not expect the strength of the pricier steel boxes.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want a mountable safe.

whatMatters.detail: A safe that can be lifted away offers little protection. Expansion bolts or mounting kits fix it to a desk or floor. Look for the words mounting hardware included in the listing, and check that your desk or floor material can hold bolts, since thin particleboard may not, and a weak anchor defeats the point.

Capacity in cubic feet shows how much you can store. A 0.23 cu ft box holds small valuables, while 0.6 cu ft fits documents. Match it to what you need to lock up, and measure a passport folder or tablet against the interior dimensions given in the listing, and leave room around items so the door closes.

Keypad safes need batteries, so a key or a USB-C input saves you after a failure. Check the listing for the backup method. The Bonsaii lists USB-C and the Amazon Basics drawer safe lists an emergency key, so you are not locked out when the cells run down, which usually happens at the worst moment.

A safe that crowds your desk gets moved, and a moved safe is one that gets unbolted. Compare the dimensions to your free space and to the drawer if you plan to hide it. Remember that the door needs room to swing open, and that a safe in a cramped corner is awkward to use daily.

Two codes or an alarm help in shared workspaces and matter if more than one person uses the safe. Check the bullets for these features. The 4.6 liter box supports two independent codes, while others list one custom code with 3 to 8 digits, so decide who needs access before buying.

faq.q: Can I bolt these to a desk?
faq.a: Most include mounting hardware, though quality varies, and the Amazon Basics Steel ships four expansion bolts. Check your desk material first, because thin particleboard may not hold bolts and needs a backing plate or a bolt into the floor instead.
Leaving a safe unmounted. It can be carried away whole, and then thieves open it at leisure. Bolt it down, even the small ones, because portability is what thieves look for.

faq.q: Is the Bonsaii worth it over a mini?
faq.a: If you store documents, yes, because it holds 0.6 cu ft and has a USB-C backup. For small valuables, the MAESTON or Yuanshikj are cheaper and smaller.

faq.q: How do I set a code?
faq.a: Follow the manual's programming steps and test the new code with the door open. The MAESTON accepts 3 to 8 digits, so choose a longer code that is not a birthday, and write it down away from the safe, ideally in a different room.

faq.q: How do I maintain a keypad safe?
faq.a: Replace batteries on a schedule and keep the backup key away from the safe. Test the keypad every few months with the door open, and keep the USB-C cable handy for the Bonsaii. Replace the battery set at the same time.

faq.q: Can a safe go in a drawer?
faq.a: The slim Amazon Basics model is listed for a drawer or desktop. Mount it to the drawer base if you can, and check the drawer is deep enough for the door to clear when it opens.

finalTake: Buy the Amazon Basics Steel safe if you want a configurable, genuinely anchored box, or the Bonsaii when documents and devices need space. Choose the slim Amazon Basics for a drawer, the dual-code box for a shared desk, and the MAESTON or Yuanshikj for small valuables on a budget. Always bolt it down.
